plan.thesis: A model is a rule fitted to some wells and judged on wells it has never seen. Associate owns A MODEL AND ITS TEST (features and a target, unseen test data, random-row and whole-well splits, the seed and the shuffle, scaling fitted on the training rows, OLS with its coefficients, standard errors and metrics, residuals by well), Professional owns VALIDATING A MODEL (ridge and the bias-variance trade, cross-validation by wells, leakage and that a random split does not always flatter, logistic regression on a stated pay rule, the confusion matrix and its ratios, ROC, AUC and log loss), Expert owns WHEN THE ENGINE REFUSES, STOPS OR EXTRAPOLATES (conditioning and the NIST reference problems, separation and its exact test, convergence and its stated rule, permutation importance and learning curves, missing-log prediction end to end and writing it back, conventions as choices). Each capstone grades only its own tier's question.

tiers.beginner: Associate: m01 what a model is (a rule fitted to data, features and a target, the Ekene wells, what a prediction is, refusals), m02 data the model has not seen (why unseen, a split by rows, a split by whole wells, the seed and the shuffle), m03 scaling on the training rows, m04 ordinary least squares, m05 fit metrics and residuals, m06 one well held out end to end. Digest sections 1 to 10, and section 26.
tiers.intermediate: Professional: m01 ridge and the bias-variance trade, m02 cross-validation by wells, m03 leakage, m04 logistic regression, m05 the confusion matrix and its ratios, m06 ROC, AUC and log loss. Digest sections 11 to 16.
tiers.advanced: Expert: m01 conditioning and the NIST reference problems, m02 separation, m03 convergence and its stated rule, m04 importance and learning curves, m05 missing-log prediction end to end, m06 reading the engine honestly. Digest sections 17 to 25.

plan.stage: FOUNDATION. run_gates.py expects numsweep_mlcore.mjs and lengths.py to refuse on the 78 stubs for their stated stub reasons; D2_STAGE=lessons flips both to must-pass.

history.position: THIS COURSE TEACHES NO REPAIR HISTORY. The engine's lead-review changes (the dual Gordan and Stiemke separation programmes, the scale-aware solveSPD, the spread-free minimum and maximum, the in-place permutation) landed before its merge and before any lesson was written; they are provenance. The digest describes the engine as it is.

scopeSeams.regression fit quality of a decline or a: OWNED BY dca and welltest (Arps parameter fitting, type-curve matching and their fit diagnostics). D2 teaches RMSE, MAE and R-squared as scores of predictions on held-out wells, and its residuals are grouped by well.
scopeSeams.Monte Carlo and uncertainty propagation: OWNED BY the uncertainty course (lib/stats sampling). The only random draws in D2 are the seeded shuffles of the splits and of permutation importance; no prediction interval is sampled.
scopeSeams.outlier statistics: OWNED BY D1 dataqc (z-score, modified z-score, Tukey fences, Hampel, Grubbs, Mahalanobis). D2 takes clean rows, refuses a missing value by name, and names D1 where a cleaning step belongs.
scopeSeams.the z-score's standard deviation: D1's z-score uses the sample SD (n - 1); D2's scaler uses the population SD (n). Digest sections 6, 25 and 26 say which and why.
scopeSeams.clustering and electrofacies: OWNED BY D3 facies (PCA, k-means, trees, kNN).
scopeSeams.forecasting a rate series: OWNED BY D4 forecastml (smoothing, rolling-origin backtests, time-ordered splits).

namingCollisions.test: rows the model was not fitted on; a whole well held out unless a random-row split is named. Section 26.
namingCollisions.standard deviation: names its divisor: the scaler's population SD against D1's sample SD. Section 26.
namingCollisions.R-squared: names its rows and its reference mean (training fit, test about the test mean, test about the training mean). Section 26.
namingCollisions.separation: the logistic property (complete, quasi-complete); a group split is a split. Section 26.
namingCollisions.importance: the loss of score for this fitted model on these rows with this seed and these repeats. Section 26.
namingCollisions.machine learning: a fitted statistical model named by its method; no AI claim. Gated by gate_vocabulary.py.

openItems.FINDINGS open question 3, the logistic s: DECIDED FOR THE COURSE: the engine rule is kept and taught as stated (Expert m03, digest section 20, with the engine's own compressibility case converging at tol 0.1 and warning at the default). No graded field depends on the stopping rule: d2_capstone.mjs refits every converged logistic field at tol 1e-14 and requires agreement within a hundredth of its tolerance, and the three-update field is asserted to stop by maxIter. A column-scaled rule would change engine iteration-count goldens and belongs to an engines PR if the lead wants it.
openItems.FINDINGS open question 4, maxCondition 1: Taught as a feature: Expert m01 shows Filip refused at the default and fitted at 1e10 to its float-design limit (digest section 18).
openItems.FINDINGS open question 2, lib/linalg sol: Not an ml.js matter (ml.js uses its own solveSPD); outside this course.
openItems.prerequisite: wave.json carries prerequisite null, as D1 does. Whether D2 should require D1 is a go-live decision for the lead.
